Alldays Orphanage UPDATE

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
After more than a decade of feeding children in the hot Limpopo sun, the Dirisanang Drop-in Centre finally have a home!

Unique Selling Point:
In March 2023 we met Paulina Manangena and Stephen Serakalala who run the Dirisanang Drop-In Centre in Alldays. For almost 2 decades they have been looking after the vulnerable children of Alldays, cooking in a corrugated iron shack, feeding kids in the hot Limpopo Sun. A Swedish benefactor, Leif Rahmqvist, was supposed to change their lives when, in 2013, he came with promises of a new building, a community centre and additional educational facilities. he raised the funds and built the building but never gave the children from the Drop-In Centre any access to the building... which he claimed... was his!


Summary:
The Mapungubwe Foundation Centre or "Orphanage" was built on municipal land, and yet the Blouberg Municipality dragged it's feet in acting on the matter.
But after our story in march, the Swedish press became involved and Rahmqvist fled SA... The building has now officially been taken over by the municipality and is available for use by the Drop-In Centre!

Press Release:


In March this year, Paulina Manengena and Stephen Serakalala were at their wits' end. For almost two decades, the twosome had been running the Dirisanang Drop-In Centre in Alldays that looks after vulnerable children. The centre was operating from a corrugated iron shack but in 2013, a Swedish benefactor, Leif Rahmqvist promised to raise funds and build a new facility for the children. The municipality made the land available and the new centre was erected. But Rahmqvist never gave the children access to the building and, for a decade, the Blouberg Municiplaity failed to act against him. After we broadcast this controversy, the Swedish press picked up the story and Rahmqvist fled South Africa. The building has now officially been taken over by the municipality and has finally been handed over to the Drop-In Centre.

Producer: Stenette Grosskopf | Presenter: Masa Kekana

Script:


​​Alldays Orphanage UPDATE Script






When we met Paulina Manengena in March, this was her life…
Paulina UPS
We have 114 kids that we take care of.


As the manager of Dirisanang Drop-In Centre in Alldays, Limpopo, she spent her weekdays in a corrugated iron shack, cooking for vulnerable children from the local community.
Paulina UPS
The kids eat outside, even when it rains. We don’t even have water.


With limited funding from the Limpopo Department of Social Development, she and her volunteers have spent the last decade making sure that the children from the community have a safe space to go after school – offering homework assistance and a daily meal.






But their lives were supposed to change for the better way back in 2013, when a wealthy Swedish benefactor - Leif Rahmqvist - arrived with promises.
Leif
Let me try to do something for those kids…


Rahmqvist pledged to build a state-of-the art facility – FOR the Drop-In Centre ON municipal land. Sizeable donations flowed in from abroad to help these children… and to fund the construction of what was to become the Mapungubwe Foundation Centre…


Paulina
I was very happy. I told myself I would be stress-free, and that everything would finally be in place.


But the fairytale did not have a happy ending. In-fighting, egos, politics and alleged fraud got in the way… The building was completed in 2014, but never handed over to the Drop-In Centre as per the initial agreement… Instead, Rahmqvist appointed his own staff to run a similar charity inside the Mapungubwe Foundation Centre building… And he continued to actively raise funds for “his” charity in Alldays….

The Drop-In Centre children were left, playing outside in the dust, eating their lunch in the hot Limpopo sun… every day, for almost a decade.
Masa & Stephen
Masa: So these are the toilets that over 100 children must use.

Stephen: Yes, we are not allowed to put a single kid in this building and there is nice toilets inside.


Stephen Serakalala, the community-elected chair of the Dirisanang Drop-In Centre NPO, was haunted by the idea that their children saw no benefit from the multi million rand building right on their doorstep.…
UPS Stephen
It’s a shame, actually it’s a shame.


And understandably the community was angry…
Joyce Lahong
The community wanted to vandalize the building because to us it is a white elephant it doesn't help us. Because the kids are suffering while the building is there.




Joyce Lehong, also a member of the Dirisanang Drop-In Centre board, felt helpless at the time
Joyce Lahong
Masa, it’s very hard to fight a person who has money, when you have nothing. Social Development comes maybe every two or three months to assess the space, but all they can do is give money, so that the kids can eat. When it comes to the building they are unable to help.


Stephen
We went to the municipality more than 50 times asking the municipality to come and intervene, to solve this problem. But they don’t help us.


In March we confronted the local Blouberg Municipality.
why is the building, built ON Municipal land, FOR the Drop-In Centre… not used by them…
Confront
Masa: What are you going to do to make sure that those children, this winter, are not inside that shack…

Frans Mphateng: As you are dealing with a case you can’t just abruptly say no today you must go…

Masa: It’s not abrupt. I’m saying this thing has been going on since 2015, 2014. That’s a long time ago, Sir.

Frans Mphateng: Those were not… they were issues that we were discussing, we were trying to resolve…

Masa: Had it been nipped in the bud then, do you think we’d be sitting in this position where you now have to get a council meeting to get rid of this man…

Frans Mphateng: Unless you realise that something really fishy is happening..

Masa: It’s really fishy… we spent 2 days..

Frans Mphateng: It’s really fishy because we can all agree. That’s why we are saying we took the matter to the HAWKS.


But much has changed since the story first aired in March…
Paulina
I am very happy to say that things have changed. The children will now be safe in this building.


Rahmqvist left the country on the eve of our broadcast, and in early August, both he and his lawyer finally resigned from the Mapungubwe Foundation Board.
Paulina
Inside we have an office space, a kitchen and even a computer room.
Paulina
The children will benefit because we never had any of these things. There is also wifi connected to the computers that will help them a lot.


Joyce Lehong has now been appointed as Treasurer of the Mapungubwe Foundation.


Joyce
Carte Blanche brought a big change. For a long time nothing happened, but finally things are changing and we can move into the building. Our dreams are coming true.
Paulina
Inside here we have tables and chairs, kitchen sinks, stoves and pots. And they say they’re going to leave everything here for the community of Alldays.


After all these years the building and equipment are in need of serious TLC

but Paulina and Joyce welcome the new challenge.

Joyce
We don’t really have the money to do the upgrades and repairs that are needed, but as always, we will find funding.

There are still questions around the donations received and the management of the Mapungubwe Foundation Centre over the past decade. Rahmqvist, his lawyer and other board members have vehemently denied any wrong-doing… The Hawks’ investigation continues.




PROMO 21”
An investigation earlier this year sparked much-needed change for a community that was about to give up hope…

UPS: Inside here we have tables and chairs, kitchen sinks, stoves and pots. And they say they’re going to leave everything here for the community of Alldays.

After more than a decade, the Dirisanang Drop-In Centre in Alldays finally has a home.
